name: application-vertical-menu
title: Vertical Menu
description: Vertical navigation list components for sidebar and panel menus, supporting plain links, badges, icons, left-border active states, accordion disclosure, and divided sections.
useWhen: Building a secondary or contextual navigation panel within an application section, such as account settings or a docs sidebar.
Navigation items require supplementary badges to show unread counts or status indicators.
Nested sub-navigation is needed within a section — accordion disclosure groups related items cleanly.
avoidWhen: Primary application navigation is needed — use a side-menu component with logo and profile areas instead.
There are only two or three navigation items — inline links or tabs are simpler.
Navigation must be accessible on mobile without a sidebar — use a bottom tab bar or hamburger drawer.
responsiveBehavior: Vertical menus are typically placed inside a sidebar that is visible at medium widths and above. On small viewports they should be hidden behind a drawer or omitted in favor of a mobile navigation pattern.
accessibility: Wrap the menu in a <nav> element with a descriptive aria-label so screen readers identify it as a distinct navigation landmark.
The active link should carry aria-current='page' or aria-current='true'.
Accordion sections using <details>/<summary> provide keyboard-accessible disclosure without JavaScript.

variants.title: Base
variants.description: Simple vertical list of navigation links with an active state highlight — the minimal pattern for settings and section navigation.
accessibility: Active link uses aria-current='page'; wrap in <nav> with an aria-label.

variants.title: Base (Dark)
variants.description: Simple vertical link list adapted for dark sidebar panels, with active state and hover highlight visible on dark backgrounds.
accessibility: Link text and active highlight colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark sidebar backgrounds.

variants.title: Base with badge
variants.description: Vertical navigation list where items carry numeric badges for unread counts, pending items, or status indicators.
accessibility: Badge counts should include a screen-reader text like 'Notifications: 5' alongside the visual number.

variants.title: Base with badge (Dark)
variants.description: Badge-carrying vertical navigation list adapted for dark surfaces, with badge colors legible on dark backgrounds.
accessibility: Badge background and text must meet contrast requirements on the dark sidebar background.

variants.title: Base with icon
variants.description: Vertical navigation list with an icon preceding each link label for faster visual scanning and category identification.
accessibility: Icons are decorative when labels are present; set aria-hidden='true' on icon elements.

variants.title: Base with icon (Dark)
variants.description: Icon-labeled vertical navigation list adapted for dark sidebar panels with icons and labels legible on dark backgrounds.
accessibility: Icon fill and label text must meet contrast requirements on dark sidebar backgrounds.

variants.title: Base with badge, icon
variants.description: Vertical navigation list combining icons and badges for the most information-dense sidebar layout — suitable for notification-heavy dashboards.
accessibility: Both icons and badges must have appropriate aria-hidden or screen-reader text; label carries primary meaning.

variants.title: Base with badge, icon (Dark)
variants.description: Icon-and-badge vertical navigation list adapted for dark surfaces with all elements visible on dark backgrounds.
accessibility: Icon, badge, and label must all meet contrast requirements on dark sidebar backgrounds.

variants.title: Base with icon, color with left border
variants.description: Icon navigation list where the active item is marked with a colored left border accent — a common pattern in admin panels and settings pages.
accessibility: Left border is a visual accent; aria-current='page' on the active link provides the semantic active state.

variants.title: Base with icon, color with left border (Dark)
variants.description: Left-border-active icon navigation list adapted for dark surfaces, with border color visible against dark backgrounds.
accessibility: Active left border color must meet contrast requirements against the dark sidebar background.

variants.title: Accordion menu
variants.description: Vertical navigation menu with expandable accordion sections using native <details>/<summary> — for grouping related links under collapsible category headers.
accessibility: Native <details>/<summary> provides keyboard-accessible open/close without JavaScript; no ARIA disclosure widget needed.

variants.title: Accordion menu (Dark)
variants.description: Accordion navigation menu adapted for dark surfaces with disclosure headers and nested link items legible on dark backgrounds.
accessibility: Summary toggle and child link colors must meet WCAG AA contrast in both collapsed and expanded states on dark backgrounds.

variants.title: Accordion menu with icon
variants.description: Accordion navigation menu with category icons on section headers and nested icon-prefixed links — the richest vertical nav pattern.
accessibility: Section header icons are decorative; <summary> text carries the accessible name for the accordion section.

variants.title: Accordion menu with icon (Dark)
variants.description: Icon-accordion navigation menu adapted for dark surfaces, keeping section headers and nested links legible on dark backgrounds.
accessibility: Icon and label colors in both section headers and nested items must meet contrast requirements on dark backgrounds.

variants.title: Base with divided sections
variants.description: Vertical navigation list split into labeled sections separated by dividers — useful for grouping unrelated navigation items within the same sidebar panel.
accessibility: Section dividers are decorative; use visible section headings or aria-label on nested lists to identify grouped link sets.

variants.title: Base with divided sections (Dark)
variants.description: Divided-section navigation list adapted for dark surfaces, with dividers and section labels visible on dark sidebar backgrounds.
accessibility: Divider colors and section heading text must meet contrast requirements against dark sidebar backgrounds.
